system.name: Lexicon viewer
system.purpose: A local web app for browsing a lexicon-conform project's cold layer (DDD-style ubiquitous language: bounded contexts, terms, invariants, aggregates, shared kernels, surfaces and regions) and its codebase in the same window. Two peer views — a reading room (catalog + detail + Monaco peek drawer) and a graph view (typeset diagram with two lenses). Single-user, single-project-at-a-time, read-only.
system.narrative:
The viewer is a *reading room*, not an IDE. A declares its as XML; persists the user's registered paths and serves files; parses the XML into a flat keyed by . From there the graph splits into two peer surfaces sharing one drawer.
The first surface is the reading room () — a three-pane shell where the left catalog navigates by bounded context, the centre column reads one entity in depth, and the right rail opens s as live Monaco peeks. The second is the graph view (): projects the same `ResolvedGraph` through one of two es, ELK lays it out, and a custom SVG renders it with the editorial aesthetic. Peeks persist across the view toggle () so the drawer never resets when the user switches.
Two things are deliberately load-bearing. The viewer never writes () — corrections go back through `lex-crystallize` in the terminal, not through this app. And the visual identity () is treated as design constraint, not decoration; capability tradeoffs lose to aesthetic ones. Everything else — the lens semantics, the path-clamp () — descends from those two commitments.

shared-kernel.name: Viewer vocabulary
shared-kernel.description: The viewer-wide nouns and invariants every context coordinates on: the fqid format, the code-anchor shape, the read-only and single-project-active commitments, the editorial aesthetic. A pragmatic kernel — strict-DDD might prefer a published-language seam between every context pair, but pinning these as a kernel keeps the definitions together with their atoms.
shared-kernel.rationale: Lifting these to one kernel keeps them traversable as a graph (every `<ref to="fqid"/>` resolves through a stable fqid) while making it explicit that no single context owns them.

term.name: lexicon-conform project
term.definition: A project that contains a top-level `lexicon/` directory of XML files conforming to schema v1.0 — `system.xml`, optional per-context files in `contexts/`, optional `surfaces/*.xml`. The viewer's input. Registered with the viewer by absolute path.

term.name: cold layer
term.definition: The structured XML files under `lexicon/` that capture vocabulary, invariants, bounded contexts, aggregates, shared kernels, and the rationale arguments that justify them. Distinct from the hot layer (per-feature plans in `lexicon/plans/`) and from code itself. The viewer reads the cold layer; it does not write it.

term.name: fqid (fully-qualified id)
term.definition: A stable string identifier for any resolved entity, unique across the graph. Forms: `system/<slug>`, `context/<slug>`, `<context>/<term>`, `<context>/invariant/<slug>`, `<context>/seam/<slug>`, `<context>/rule/<slug>`, `<context>/aggregate/<slug>`, `<context>/module/<slug>`, `kernel/<slug>`, `kernel/<slug>/<term>`, `kernel/<slug>/invariant/<slug>`, `surface/<slug>`, `surface/<slug>/<region>`. Used as React keys, graph node IDs, route params (`/p/:id/<fqid>`).
term.equality: By string value. Two fqids are the same iff their strings match.

term.name: code anchor
term.definition: A pointer from a cold-layer entity into a code file: `{file, lineStart?, lineEnd?, symbol?}`. Lives on `Term.symbols`, `Invariant.constrainsCode`, and `Region.implementation` (inline variant carries `file/lineStart/lineEnd`, component variant carries `import` with optional `file`). The viewer renders anchors as badges that open the file in a Monaco peek.
term.equality: Structural — same file, same line range, same symbol.

term.name: peek
term.definition: A Monaco editor instance opened in a side drawer to read the file behind a code anchor, with the anchor's line range highlighted. Multiple peeks stack vertically. State lives in a React context (`PeekProvider`) so peeks persist across view changes (reading room ↔ graph view). Read-only — the peek shows the file as-on-disk; the viewer never writes.

invariant.name: viewer is read-only
invariant.statement: The viewer never writes to cold-layer XML, never modifies code, and never mutates the user's filesystem outside `lexicon-viewer.db`. Corrections go through `lex-crystallize` running in the user's terminal, not through the viewer.
invariant.rationale: Editing in the viewer would duplicate `lex-crystallize`'s deliberate propose-then-apply discipline, and likely badly — the viewer has no access to the full conversational context that makes crystallization good. Keep the viewer a *reading room*, not an IDE.

invariant.name: one project active at a time
invariant.statement: The browser loads exactly one project's `ResolvedGraph` at a time. The search index, recency cache, and peek state are scoped to that project. Switching projects reloads everything from scratch.
invariant.rationale: Single-project scope keeps the in-browser index small (linear scan over hundreds of entities), routing simple (`/p/:id/...`), and the mental model uncluttered. Cross-project features (if ever) would be a separate surface, not a graph-layer concern.

invariant.name: editorial-meets-blueprint aesthetic
invariant.statement: The viewer's visual identity (Fraunces + IBM Plex Mono on ink/vellum with oxide accents, sharp geometry, hairline rules, no rounded badges, no purple defaults) is load-bearing — a correct-but-generic viewer would feel like a downgrade from the XML it renders. Canonical vocabulary and component primitives live in ; surfaces consume from there rather than declaring their own colors, fonts, or shapes.
invariant.rationale:
The aesthetic is the differentiator. When adding a feature, push the typography and edge styling until it reads as "extension of the existing viewer," not "bolted on." If a tradeoff arises between capability and aesthetic, the aesthetic wins.
The layout layer (ELK.js) and rendering layer (custom SVG) were chosen for this reason: Cytoscape / react-flow / d3-force all *work*, but their default node aesthetics fight the editorial direction. Layout-only ELK plus our own SVG keeps full control of typography and edge styling. The trade is engineering cost — we own pan/zoom, hover-dim, selection state, and routing — and it's been worth it.

deliberate-omission.topic: Editing the cold layer in the viewer
deliberate-omission.reason: Corrections route back through `lex-crystallize` in the user's terminal, not through this app. Adding an in-viewer editor would duplicate the crystallize discipline (propose, get user yes, apply) and likely badly — the viewer has no access to the conversational context that makes crystallization good. See .
deliberate-omission.trigger: A clear use case where terminal round-trip blocks routine fixes (e.g. typo in a `name` field for a heavily-renamed entity).
Crystallize itself moves into a non-terminal context.

deliberate-omission.reason: The browser loads exactly one project's at a time (). Cross-project features — finding every shared term that mentions a concept, diffing two projects' contexts — would change the routing shape (`/p/:id/...` no longer scopes everything) and inflate the in-browser index. Not blocking; no real demand yet.
deliberate-omission.trigger: Two or more projects start sharing a meaningful term vocabulary.
A user asks "where in any of my projects did I…".

deliberate-omission.reason: Today the user clicks Refresh; the loader re-reads and the is cleared globally. A filesystem watcher would push updates automatically, but the manual click is a strong intentional signal () and avoids partial-write races on long XML edits. Polish-bundle plan considers this; not committed.
deliberate-omission.trigger: User complains the click cadence breaks flow during heavy crystallize sessions.
